- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially after 1–2 bullish sentiment spikes — leading to overshoot; apply smoothing filter or lag 1 correction.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or oscillating), model often fails to revert to historical mean; use 30-day moving average as anchor for correction.
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to overestimate upward momentum; cap forecast growth rate at 2–3% per week unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price fails to rise (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of +0.67 sentiment with flat or declining price), reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model often overfits recent noise; use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days to stabilize forecast.
